hypothesis: Theorem SA-1 predicts that four canonical inductive-bias regimes each satisfy local-separation and cross-u coherence on the 4-bit Boolean world; the finest common refinement of each antecedent's local screens equals the true Z-partition.

controls.description: The reference partition Z is computed directly from the ground-truth latent map latent_z(x) = (x_0 ^ x_1, x_2 ^ x_3), independent of any candidate quotient.
The partition_intersection helper labels each world by the tuple of block indices across all input partitions and groups by that label; verified by construction to be the finest common refinement.
partition_refines(P, P) returns True for every non-trivial P — a sanity check on the refinement predicate.

gates.criterion: Every local screen for every antecedent is a non-trivial partition of X (2 <= |blocks| <= |X| - 1).
The finest common refinement of each antecedent's local screens refines the true Z-partition.
For LinearICA, SparseLinearICA, and AuxIVAE, the intersection is exactly the Z-partition.
For InterventionalCRL, the intersection refines the Z-partition.
